info.title: C2C E-Commerce API
info.description: RESTful API for the C2C (consumer-to-consumer) e-commerce marketplace. Supports user authentication, listings management, orders, reviews, and categories.

bearerAuth.description: Enter the JWT token obtained from POST /api/auth/login

path.description: Dot-separated ancestor ids, including this category.

post.description: Authenticates a user with email and password and returns a JWT token.

429.description: Too many login attempts from this IP

post.description:
Validates the JWT and clears the httpOnly `auth_token` cookie, ending
the browser session. The JWT is stateless, so a token held outside the
cookie stays valid until it expires.

200.description: Logout confirmed and auth cookie cleared

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's profile from the database.

Validates `state` against the signed transaction cookie, exchanges the code, resolves or creates the user, and issues the session cookies. The access token is never placed in the redirect URL: it would land in browser history, server logs and the `Referer` header. The client picks the session up from the cookies.

302.description: Redirect into the app on success, or to /login?error=<code>

429.description: Too many attempts from this IP

get.description: Redirects to the provider's authorization endpoint and stores the transaction (state, PKCE verifier, nonce, returnTo) in a short-lived signed cookie. Google receives a PKCE challenge; GitHub OAuth Apps do not support PKCE and receive `state` only.

parameters.name: returnTo
parameters.description: Same-site path to land on after signing in. External origins are ignored.

429.description: Too many attempts from this IP

delete.description: Removes the caller's link to a provider. Refuses when it is the caller's last remaining credential -- an OAuth-only account unlinking its only provider would have no way back in.

404.description: No such link for this user

409.description: Would remove the caller's last credential

post.summary: Attach an external identity to an existing password account
post.description: Completes the collision flow started by the OAuth callback. Requires the signed `link_tx` cookie **and** the existing account's password (decision D9): a provider-supplied email address is not proof of ownership, so the account's own credential is what authorises the link.

get.summary: Which OAuth2 providers this deployment offers
get.description: Public. The login page renders a button per entry, so a provider without credentials never shows a button that would 404. Returns only provider names -- no client ids, no redirect URIs.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token
post.description: Reads the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie, rotates it, and returns a fresh 15-minute access token. Refresh tokens are single-use: presenting one that has already been rotated is treated as theft and revokes every token in its family, forcing a new login.

200.description: A new access token, with both session cookies refreshed

401.description: Missing, unknown, expired, already-used, or concurrently-rotated refresh token. The reason is deliberately not distinguished in the response.

post.description: Creates a new user account and returns a JWT token.

429.description: Too many registration attempts from this IP

put.description: Updates an existing category. Admin only. Partial updates supported.

delete.description: Permanently removes a category. Admin only.

get.description: Returns all categories sorted alphabetically by name. Public endpoint.

post.description: Creates a new product category. Admin only.

parentId.description: Parent category. Omit or send null for a root.

get.description: Public. Streams the stored bytes same-origin. Storage keys are random, so a URL never outlives the bytes it names and the response is cached immutably.

delete.summary: Remove a photo from a listing

post.summary: Upload a photo to a listing
post.description: Multipart upload of a single `file`. The type is decided from the file's magic bytes, never its declared Content-Type or filename, and the image is re-encoded to WebP — which also strips EXIF, including any GPS coordinates. Owner or admin only. At most 8 images per listing, 5 MB each.

400.description: Not a JPEG, PNG or WebP

patch.description: Body `{ order: number[] }` — image ids in their new order. Owner or admin.

get.description: Returns all reviews for a specific listing, including the reviewer name.

post.summary: Create a review for a listing
post.description:
Adds a review to a listing. Only buyers can review.
A user can only submit one review per listing, and only for a listing
they have actually purchased.

403.description: Not a buyer, or the buyer has no completed order containing this listing (statuses paid, shipped, completed or approved).

get.description:
Returns a single listing with seller and category names.
Only active listings are visible publicly; the owner or admin can see any status.

put.description: Updates an existing listing. Only the owner seller or an admin may update. Partial updates supported.

delete.description: Permanently removes a listing. Only the owner seller or an admin may delete.

get.description:
Nearest neighbours of a listing by embedding cosine distance. Public — this needs no user history at all, so it works on a visitor's first page view.
Only `active` listings with a computed embedding are returned, and the source listing is never among them. A listing whose own embedding has not been computed yet answers `200` with an empty array rather than an error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The listing to find neighbours for

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many neighbours to return (capped at 20)

parameters.name: sameCategoryOnly
parameters.description: Restrict results to the source listing's category. A source with no category returns an empty array under this filter rather than ignoring it.

post.summary: Generate a listing description with a language model
post.description:
Turns a product title, and optionally some keywords and a category, into a marketplace description the seller can edit before saving. Nothing is stored — the client posts the edited text to the normal create route.
The model is instructed not to invent specifications or prices and not to include contact details, but the output is a **draft for a human to review**, not a statement of fact about the item.

model.description: The model that produced the text.

400.description: Invalid body — title length, keyword count or keyword length

403.description: Authenticated, but not a seller or admin

429.description: Generation quota exhausted for this account

502.description: The language model was unreachable, timed out, or returned nothing

get.description:
Returns paginated active listings with optional filters.
When `sellerId` matches the authenticated seller (or the caller is an
admin), non-active listings are included too, for the seller dashboard.
All other callers only ever receive active listings.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Category id. Includes every descendant category, so filtering by a parent returns listings filed under its subcategories.

parameters.name: sellerId
parameters.description: Filter by seller ID. Returns all statuses only when it is the authenticated seller's own ID; otherwise active listings only.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search term. In `keyword` mode it matches the title (case-insensitive contains); in `semantic` and `hybrid` mode it is embedded and compared against listing vectors.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
How `search` is interpreted.
`keyword` (default) is the original behaviour and is unchanged.
`semantic` embeds the query and ranks by cosine similarity, returning only matches at or above a similarity floor of 0.25. Listings whose embedding has not been computed are excluded.
`hybrid` runs the keyword and semantic arms independently and fuses them with reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60), so a listing matching both outranks one matching either alone. A listing with no embedding is still reachable through the keyword arm.
**`total` differs by mode.** In `keyword` mode it counts every row matching the filters. In `semantic` and `hybrid` mode it counts only ranked candidates — rows above the similarity floor, or the fused candidate set — so it is not the size of the table.
With no `search` term, `semantic` and `hybrid` behave as `keyword`: there is nothing to embed.

semantic.summary: Semantic mode adds a similarity to each row

post.description: Creates a new marketplace listing. Requires seller or admin role.

get.description: Returns a single order with its items. Only the buyer who placed it or an admin can view.

put.description:
Updates the status of an order.
- **Admin**: can change to any status.
- **Seller**: can only approve/reject pending orders that contain their listings.
When a seller approves, their listings in the order are marked as "sold".

400.description: Validation error or invalid status transition

delete.description: Permanently removes an order and its items. Admin only.

get.description:
Buyers see only their own orders. Admins see all orders.
Results are sorted by creation date (newest first).

post.description:
Creates a new order from one or more active listings.
Only buyers can place orders. Total is calculated server-side.

404.description: Listing not found or not active

get.description:
Returns orders that contain at least one item from the authenticated seller's
listings. Each order includes only the items belonging to the seller, plus
the buyer's name and email. Requires seller or admin role.

get.summary: Listings recommended for the authenticated user
get.description:
Personalised from data the marketplace already has — what the user ordered and what they reviewed. No browsing or view history is tracked.
A user with no usable history gets the newest active listings from the most populated categories instead. The `strategy` field says which of the two happened, so a client never presents a popular list as a personal one.
Listings the user already ordered, their own listings, and anything not `active` are excluded from both strategies.

strategy.description: `personalised` — ranked against a taste vector built from the user's orders and reviews. `popular` — the cold-start fallback.

delete.description: Permanently removes a review. Only the reviewer or an admin can delete.

get.description: Returns a single user profile. Admin can view any user; regular users can only view themselves.

put.description:
Updates a user profile. Partial updates supported.
- **Self**: can update name, phoneNumber, password.
- **Admin**: can additionally update role.

delete.description: Permanently removes a user account. Admin only.

get.description: Returns all users sorted by creation date. Admin only. Passwords are excluded.
